description: Group examinations by patient ID, with the examinations lacking an ID forming one group that counts toward the total and the average share; list up to 10 above-average groups by excess share.

a.request: Group the examination records by patient `ID`, with examinations that have no patient ID forming one group of their own. For each group, count its examinations and work out that count as a fraction of the total over all groups. For the groups whose fraction is above the average fraction across groups, list the ID, the number of examinations, the fraction, and how much the fraction exceeds the average, sorted by that excess from largest to smallest, top 10 only, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), f AS (SELECT ID, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS fraction FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(fraction) AS avg_fraction FROM f) SELECT f.ID, f.cnt AS num_examinations, f.fraction, f.fraction - a.avg_fraction AS excess FROM f, a WHERE f.fraction > a.avg_fraction ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Break the examination records down by patient ID. Which IDs have an above-average share of the examinations? Show the ID, its number of examinations, its share of the total, and how far above the average share it is, listing the top 10 by that margin from largest to smallest, unrounded. Group examinations by patient ID, with the examinations lacking an ID forming one group that counts toward the total and the average share; list up to 10 above-average groups by excess share.
c.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), t AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM g) SELECT g.ID AS ID, g.cnt AS num_examinations, CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total AS share, CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total - 1.0 / t.n AS excess_share FROM g, t WHERE CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total > 1.0 / t.n ORDER BY excess_share DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: Group Examination records by patient ID, treating records with a NULL ID as one additional group that counts toward the total and the average share, then compute each group's examination count and its share of all examination records. Keep the groups whose share is above the average share (1 divided by the number of groups, NULL group included). Return up to the top 10 by excess share, from largest to smallest, with the ID, examination count, share, and excess over the average share, all unrounded
b.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), t AS (SELECT CAST(SUM(cnt) AS REAL) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM g) SELECT g.ID AS ID, g.cnt AS examination_count, g.cnt / t.total AS share, g.cnt / t.total - 1.0 / t.n AS excess_share FROM g, t WHERE g.cnt / t.total > 1.0 / t.n ORDER BY excess_share DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Break the examination records down by patient ID, treating examinations that have no patient ID as one additional group that counts toward the total number of examinations and toward the average share. Which groups have an above-average share of the examinations? For each, show the patient ID (or the missing-ID group), its number of examinations, its share of the total, and how far its share is above the average share. List up to the top 10 by that margin, from largest to smallest, with values unrounded.
d.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), t AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, COUNT(*) AS ngroups FROM g) SELECT CASE WHEN g.ID IS NULL THEN 'missing ID' ELSE CAST(g.ID AS TEXT) END AS patient_id, g.cnt AS num_examinations, CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total AS share, CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total - 1.0 / t.ngroups AS margin_above_average FROM g, t WHERE CAST(g.cnt AS REAL) / t.total > 1.0 / t.ngroups ORDER BY margin_above_average DESC LIMIT 10
